messages.subject: Re: R,JRI and eclipse configuration
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Can you try to give some arguments to the Rengine :

Rengine re=new Rengine(new String[]{ "--vanilla" }, false, null);

Specially when you can read this from the documentation :

     args - arguments to be passed to R. Please note that R requires the 
presence of certain arguments (e.g. --save or --no-save or equivalents), 
so passing an empty list usually doesn't work.


You really should use the new high level API, based on the REngine class 
[1]. Just download the REngine.jar and JRIEngine.jar files from 
http://www.rforge.net/JRI/files/

Romain

[1] 
http://www.rforge.net/org/docs/index.html?org/rosuda/REngine/REngine.html

messages.subject: Re: wont JGR run on R installed on a pendrive
messages.subject_clean: wont JGR run on R installed on a pendrive
messages.body_plain:
On Dec 16, 2009, at 3:34 AM, Duleep Samuel wrote:

> Sir, I have installed R 2.10 on a pendrive, when I run JGR.exe it just refuses to start, can anybody help, thanks, Samuel, Bangalore

Details?
Note that you'll need the entire R and the supporting packages (JGR and its dependencies) installed on that machine regardless of what's on the pen drive. R (and Java) must be registered in the registry of that machine, otherwise you'll need to specify it manually when starting JGR.

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: Problems Installing and using JGR on Vista
messages.subject_clean: Problems Installing and using JGR on Vista
messages.body_plain:
I am surprised at how difficult it is to get JGR running on Vista.

Gabor Grothendieck, back in June, talked of his struggles, but then I saw nothing else about it, so I assumed it was solved.
http://mailman.rz.uni-augsburg.de/pipermail/stats-rosuda-devel/2009q2/001093.html

However, when I tried to install it today, I ran into similar problems.

Installed R 2.10.1, it runs fine, installed JGR's packages from there.  Then, wanted to complete the install by running the JGR exe.

Just running JGR from a command window gives the following debug:

"
System: Version 6.0 (build 6001), platform 2 [Service Pack 1]

JGR loader version 1.61 (build Jul 23 2008)

parseParams> 1 parameters parsed.
parseParams par 10> "--debug"
> rhome="C:\Program Files\R\R-2.10.1"
> srhome="C:\PROGRA~1\R\R-210~1.1"

getPkgVersion(rJava): not found
getPkgVersion(JavaGD): not found
getPkgVersion(iplots): not found
getPkgVersion(iWidgets): not found
need to install: "JGR","rJava","JavaGD","iplots","iWidgets"
creating script file 'C:\Users\Michael\AppData\Local\Temp\instPkg.r'
CreateProcess("C:\PROGRA~1\R\R-210~1.1\bin\R.exe","-q --no-restore --no-save --internet2 < C:\Users\Michael\AppData\Local\Temp\instPkg.r 2> C:\Users\Michael\AppData\Local\Temp\instPkg.r.out",...)
 - return value: 1
 - waiting for R to finish
 - R batch process has exit code 1
Package installation result is 0
"

The packages are all there, and I can use RGUI's package manager to run JGR:

"Loading required package: rJava
Loading required package: JavaGD
Loading required package: iplots

Please use the corresponding JGR launcher to start JGR.
Run JGR() for details. You can also use JGR(update=TRUE) to update JGR.
"

So, I try to Update, and see what happens:
"
> JGR(update=TRUE)
Warning in install.packages(c("JGR", "rJava", "JavaGD", "iplots"), lt, c(cran,  :
  'lib = "C:\PROGRA~1\R\R-210~1.1/library"' is not writable
Error in install.packages(c("JGR", "rJava", "JavaGD", "iplots"), lt, c(cran,  : 
  unable to install packages
In addition: Warning message:
In if (cran == "@CRAN@") cran <- "http://cran.r-project.org/" :
  the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used
"

This is my first use of R on Vista.  Is this a common problem with R on Vista or a problem with JGR?  http://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/base/rw-FAQ.html#Does-R-run-under-Windows-Vista_003f gives some clues, but I am mostly confused by all this.

My Rhome (via > getwd()) appears to be "C:/Users/Michael/Documents"; is that part of the problem?  I selected some kind of "user library" which was new; I hadn't seen that in earlier R installs.  It's confusing to have my R in one directory, and a bunch of libraries somewhere else.

Suggestions appreciated!

Thanks, 

Michael Wexler

messages.body_plain:
Michael,

please have a look at R for Windows FAQ 2.24:
http://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/base/rw-FAQ.html
that may be the issue.

I don't have Vista so I can neither verify it nor try to find a work around. If someone wants to donate a Vista of Win7 license we may be able to support those systems but currently we can't unless users report and test what's necessary.

Thanks,
Simon
